program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the source mug's requested move to the right of the headphones complete, incomplete with visible progress, or not made?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if visual correspondence establishes that the source mug is positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image, satisfying the requested move. Fail if the source mug is identifiable and remains at its source-side position with no visible progress toward the right. Also fail if the source mug is identifiable and evidence establishes that it has not moved toward the right, even if unrelated objects or edits are present. If the source mug's appearance or location has visibly changed, or a plausible corresponding mug has moved toward the right while remnants remain, treat this as incomplete progress and fail rather than pass. Do not count a right-side mug alone as completion, or infer no progress solely from a pale mug left of the headphones or an indistinct blue patch at the source location. Use unknown only when source-to-edited correspondence or whether any progress occurred cannot be determined from the images.
nodes.binding: Compare the source image's light-blue mug—including its body shape, handle, appearance, scale, and original position left of the headphones—with all mug-like objects and visible remnants in the edited image. Assess the pale mug left of the headphones, the mug right of them, and the blue-looking blurred patch at far left as possible correspondence evidence. Altered color, size, or appearance alone does not rule out identity; neither the patch nor the left mug conclusively establishes identity or lack of movement. Determine whether the source mug is visibly to the right of the headphones, has plausibly moved toward the right but remains short of the requested position, or shows no discernible progress. Base the decision on source-to-edited visual evidence and the requested move, not mug count or right-side position alone; retain unknown if correspondence or progress remains genuinely indeterminate.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The trace’s evidence supports that the original mug is no longer clearly identifiable, but it does not establish “no progress”: the blue blurred patch at the source location and the changed mug-like objects leave correspondence and partial movement unresolved. The binding already warns against treating the patch, left mug, or right-side mug as conclusive; make the decision criterion operationally enforce that warning by comparing source-specific features and spatial change, and distinguish incomplete visible progress from no progress. In particular, do not infer no progress merely because the source mug is not established as the right-side mug or because completion is unproven. The reference label is partial, so investigate whether the changed appearance/position of a plausible corresponding mug indicates movement short of the target, while retaining unknown if correspondence truly cannot be determined; do not force partial from the label. This was a valid, queried visual evaluation with no dependency or transport failure, so the issue is semantic classification, not execution.

observations.evidence: The source light-blue mug is left of the headphones. In the edited image, a pale mug remains left of the headphones, while a separate mug is to their right; the source mug’s distinctive light-blue appearance is also visible as a blurred patch at far left. The source mug is not established as the right-side mug, and the visible evidence indicates no completed move to the right of the headphones.

Determine whether the right-side mug is a plausible transformed continuation of the source mug, rather than relying on its position alone; also assess whether the pale mug left of the headphones or the blue blur at far left indicates the source mug remains or has moved.
findings.evidence: The source has one large light-blue mug left of the headphones. The edit shows a pale mug left of the headphones, another mug to their right, and a blue blurred patch farther left. The right-side mug is not visibly light blue, and the edited image contains multiple possible correspondences.
findings.rationale: The existing check notes that the source mug is not established as the right-side mug, but its evidence does not resolve whether the right-side mug could be a transformed source mug or whether the left mug and blue patch are remnants. This focused correspondence investigation is needed to judge completion versus partial progress or no progress without treating color change or mug count as decisive.
